title: Initial management of acute bacterial meningitis in adults: summary of IDSA guidelines

claims.text: In patients aged 2-50 years, the common bacterial meningitis pathogens are N. meningitidis and S. pneumoniae.
In patients aged 50 years and older, the pathogens broaden to include S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, L. monocytogenes, and aerobic gram-negative bacilli.
claims.byte_quote: S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, L. monocytogenes, aerobic gram-negative bacilli

claims.text: After neurosurgery or with a CSF shunt/device, likely organisms include S. aureus, coagulase-negative staphylococci, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and other gram-negative bacilli.
claims.byte_quote: S. aureus, coagulase negative Staphylococci, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and other gram-negative bacilli

claims.text: Host factors such as immune suppression and recent neurosurgical procedures including ventricular shunts influence the presentation of bacterial meningitis.
claims.byte_quote: The presentation of bacterial meningitis is also influenced by host factors, such as immune suppression or recent neurosurgical procedures including ventricular shunts.

claims.text: Only 44%-51% of patients have the classic triad of fever, neck stiffness, and impaired consciousness.
claims.byte_quote: 44% to 51% have the triad of fever, neck stiffness, and impaired consciousness.

claims.text: CSF Gram stain is positive in 60%-90% of patients, with a specificity of at least 97%.
claims.byte_quote: Positive in 60%-90% of patients with a specificity of ≥97%.

claims.text: Empiric therapy for ages 2-50 is vancomycin plus ceftriaxone or cefotaxime.
Empiric therapy for ages over 50 adds ampicillin: vancomycin, ampicillin, and ceftriaxone or cefotaxime.
claims.byte_quote: Vancomycin, ampicillin, and ceftriaxone or cefotaxime

claims.text: Adult vancomycin dose is 15 mg/kg every 8-12 hours, adjusted to maintain trough concentrations of 15-20 ug/mL.
claims.byte_quote: 15 mg/kg q8-12h adjusted to maintain trough concentrations of 15-20 µg/mL

claims.text: Adult ceftriaxone dose is 2 g every 12 hours.
Adjunctive dexamethasone dose is 0.15 mg/kg every 6 hours for 2-4 days, given before antibiotics in pneumococcal cases.
